name: Jeremy Corbyn
role: UK MP for Islington North (since 1983); Labour leader (2015-2020); Your Party parliamentary leader (2026)
summary: Corbyn is a democratic socialist who favours public ownership of utilities and railways, higher taxes on the wealthy, strong trade unions and an end to austerity. He is a long-standing anti-war and anti-nuclear campaigner who opposes Trident, was sceptical of NATO and backs Palestinian statehood and self-determination movements, though he has accepted some compromises as Labour leader.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In his 2018 conference speech he called the NHS a beacon for those fighting for universal healthcare free at the point of need, paid for through general taxation.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: In the March 2023 Budget debate he urged a £15 an hour minimum wage; in 2016 he pledged to raise the minimum wage to a real living wage.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In 2016 he said people are fed up with a 'so-called free market system' that produced grotesque inequality and stagnating living standards; in 2023 he argued a privately run energy system would not deliver green investment.

public-ownership.rationale: He called for energy companies to be taken into public ownership (2023), for water to be returned to public ownership (2026) and backed public ownership of the railways in his 2015 and 2016 speeches.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: In 2023 he called for a wealth tax and a 50% rate on the top 1% of earners, and in 2025 asked whether society was content not to have a wealth tax.

unions-good.rationale: In 2016 he pledged to repeal the Trade Union Act and 'set unions free to do their job'; in 2015 he called the Trade Union Bill a fundamental attack on human rights.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He repeatedly argued for tighter control of private firms: banks (2016 pledge never to let reckless bankers wreck the economy), PFI contractors, water and energy companies.

cut-welfare.rationale: He campaigned against cuts to tax credits and disability benefits and argued in the Commons for ending the two-child limit and the benefit cap.

worker-ownership.rationale: In 2018 he endorsed Inclusive Ownership Funds to share rewards with workers and called for new forms of ownership; he has wanted workforce representatives to run public water companies.

empower-police-military.rationale: He favoured more police numbers (2018) but opposed rising military spending and arms expenditure, so evidence on the combined statement is mixed.

rehabilitation.rationale: In 2019 he said too many people are in prison on very short sentences for non-violent offences and that rehabilitation proposals should be examined.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In 2015 he promised to bring same-sex marriage to Northern Ireland.

abortion-legal.rationale: He voted for Northern Ireland abortion regulations (2021), urged extension of abortion rights in 2018 and signed a 2017 call for buffer zones around clinics.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He voted against the Rwanda, Nationality and Borders and Immigration and Asylum bills and defended refugees and migrants in the Commons.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: In 2026 he asked for UN reform and funding so it could play a real role in ending conflicts; in 2015 he spoke of strengthening the UN.

nation-first.rationale: He criticised Trump's 'aggressive nationalism' for turning away from international cooperation, and committed to engagement with international institutions.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He opposed the Kosovo, Libya and Syria interventions, but in 2015 named East Timor's UN peacekeeping as justified, so evidence is mixed.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: In 2018 he called climate change the biggest threat facing humanity and announced a programme of investment to cut emissions 60% by 2030.

expand-nuclear.rationale: In 2022 he said he was 'not a great fan of nuclear power' and doesn't think it is a great direction to go down.

tax-inheritance.rationale: In 2015 he attacked the government for cutting inheritance tax for 60,000 of the wealthiest families while cutting child tax credits.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He proposed a National Investment Bank and in 2018 said government should not be held back from supporting cutting-edge industries by state-aid rules.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He would prefer a republic but accepts the monarchy's popularity and has said he is not fighting it.

right-to-secede.rationale: On Scotland he said he recognises the right of people to decide on independence and it would be wrong for Westminster to block a referendum.

direct-action.rationale: He works through Parliament but has defended direct action and protest (2025 Palestine Action debate), so evidence points both ways.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In 2018 he said Labour supports a two-state solution with a secure Israel, but he also condemned Israel's nation-state law and occupation.

workplace-democracy.rationale: In 2018 he said a worker's position is on the board and that workers deserve a real say in company decisions.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: In 2015 he said that with interest rates so low it was the time for public investment, and he promoted an investing-to-grow strategy against austerity.

national-self-determination.rationale: He said Kurdish self-determination must be accepted (2016), backed Kashmiri self-determination (2025) and Palestinian statehood.

force-without-un.rationale: In 2004 he signed a motion criticising the Kosovo intervention for lacking UN Security Council sanction, and he opposed British military action in Syria in 2018.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: In 2019 he asked the Prime Minister to ban fracking and in 2023 criticised new oil drilling and fracking as incompatible with climate commitments.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: In 2016 he said people are shut out by a political stitch-up, and in 2026 he said private donations had corrupted the political system.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He pledged truth and justice for Orgreave and Hillsborough families and in 2025 welcomed the Labour-pledged Orgreave inquiry in the Commons; he has also urged an investigation of Blair over Iraq.

priority-to-poor.rationale: In the 2025 welfare debate he said that if supporting disabled people cost more, 'so be it', and he regularly framed policy around poverty.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: In 2016 and 2017 he criticised council homes being sold off without replacement and noted 40% of right-to-buy homes were now privately rented.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: He opposed the Trade Union Bill in 2015, voted against rejecting Lords amendments to the Trade Union Bill in 2016, and against rail minimum service levels in 2023 and promised repeal of the Trade Union Act.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: In 2026 he asked whether government could say it would control food prices if they began rising sharply.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: He backed conference deciding policy as leader, but as a backbencher he routinely voted against his party whip.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: In 2013 he said he did not believe in continuing defence alliances; he has since said he would seek to restrict NATO's role rather than leave.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: He is a longstanding supporter of a united Ireland, as he reiterated in 2015.

death-penalty.rationale: In 2019 he expressed alarm at a Home Secretary who supports the death penalty and asked for assurance capital punishment would not return; in 2015 he condemned Saudi Arabia's use of it.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: In a 2019 climate debate he called for serious steps on debt relief and cancellation for countries struggling with international debts.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He regularly criticised cuts to overseas aid, saying in 2025 they would hit the poorest people in the poorest countries.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: He campaigned to scrap Trident and in 2015 said £100 billion on a new generation of nuclear weapons was not the right way forward.

flat-income-tax.rationale: He backed higher income tax rates on top earners (a 50% rate on the top 1% in 2023), the opposite of a flat rate.

refugee-return.rationale: He has pressed for the right of return of the Chagossians, which he said the 2026 Bill won for the outer islands, and called for Tamils' return in 2009.

no-bailouts.rationale: He criticised the bailout of the banking system in 2018, yet in 2015 urged the government to step in to save a steel plant and its jobs.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: He backed the 2024 bill removing hereditary peers, voting against a reasoned amendment to it, and prefers a republic.

elective-rulers.rationale: He has said he would prefer Britain to become a republic, though it is not a battle he is fighting.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: In 2013 he warned against sending weapons to Syrian opposition groups, citing Afghanistan's mujahideen.

corporate-influence.rationale: In 2026 he warned in the Commons that private donations from health interests and lobbying money corrupt democracy, and in 2016 said a political stitch-up shuts most people out of power.

non-intervention.rationale: He opposes Western military intervention (Iraq, Libya, Venezuela) but backs UN peacekeeping, arms embargoes and ICC action, so the absolute statement is mixed.

national-law-over-international.rationale: He argued in 2024 that Britain should respect the ICJ and international law, and welcomed staying in the European Convention on Human Rights.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: He criticised private-sector involvement and PFI contracts in the NHS and called for services to be brought back into public hands.

holocaust-denial.rationale: In 2026 he referred in the Commons to the horrors of the Holocaust against the Jewish people as a historical fact children are taught.

participatory-democracy.rationale: In 2018 he said Labour would democratise the economy and public services, putting workers on boards; he backs community and workforce roles in running public water.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: In 2022 he said excluding trans people from a conversion therapy ban was wrong and called for a total ban.

assisted-dying.rationale: He voted against the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill at second reading (2024) and third reading (2025).

islam-incompatible.rationale: In 2018 he said Labour will never stay silent on Islamophobia and in 2026 condemned its growth; he did not present Muslims or Islam as incompatible with British values.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: In 2015 he said there is no contradiction between working for peace and doing what is necessary to keep Britain safe, and commissioned a defence review.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: In 2013 he called for better relations with all power blocs rather than NATO rearmament.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He has argued that private wealth and donations corrupt politics and that deep inequality fuels racism and a crisis of democracy (2018 speech).

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He promised 10,000 more police officers (2018) and 3,000 more prison officers (2017 Commons speech).

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: He voted for the 1998 Northern Ireland Bill implementing the Good Friday Agreement, saying he looked forward to peace and reconciliation.

rent-control.rationale: In 2016 he pledged Labour would control private rents, and in 2023 called for an immediate rent freeze and rent control.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: He has opposed Trident's renewal and nuclear weapons held in Britain for decades, including in his 2015 speech and 2016 Trident debate.

recognise-genocide.rationale: In the 2013 Commons debate on Kurdish genocide he supported recognising the 1988 genocide in Iraq and said recognition helps protect minorities.

local-essentials-public.rationale: He argued in 2026 that water should be in popular public ownership and in 2024 that private providers undermine the NHS.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He has opposed nearly all overseas military action and says he would prefer diplomacy, though he accepts some UN-backed conflicts as justified.

free-public-college.rationale: As leader he proposed scrapping tuition fees and restoring maintenance grants in 2015 and 2017.

arms-reduction.rationale: In the 2013 NATO debate he said peace would be achieved by spending less on weapons; in 2026 he again criticised $2.8 trillion in arms spending.

collective-bargaining.rationale: In 2024 he asked the minister to progress towards full sectoral bargaining for civil servants.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: He led the 2015 campaign against cuts to tax credits and said in 2016 that the campaign had knocked the government back.

student-debt-relief.rationale: In 2017 he pledged to investigate cancelling the student debts of recent graduates.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: He has long backed unilateral nuclear disarmament, voted against Trident renewal in 2016 and said threatening mass murder is not a legitimate way to deal with international relations.

voter-id.rationale: He voted against the Elections Bill at second and third reading, which introduced voter ID.

women-suffrage.rationale: His 2018 speech marked the centenary of the Representation of the People Act giving women the vote.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: In 2026 he argued ICC arrest warrants against Israeli officials must be enforced and he has called for Blair to be investigated for war crimes.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: In a 2025 debate he said the people of Kashmir should be able to decide their own future, and in 2023 criticised Morocco for not allowing a Western Sahara referendum.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: He voted for the January 2022 opposition motion to cut VAT on household energy bills.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: He backed universal provision, such as universal free childcare (2018) and a universal NHS, rather than targeting only the poorest.

notes: Hansard covers 2001 onward and the votes API 2016 onward; earlier positions rest on Wikipedia. On NATO he argued in 2013 against defence alliances, then said as leader he would seek to restrict its role; the later position is used. On the EU he opposed membership historically but backed Remain in 2016 and a second referendum in 2019. Answers that rest only on a vote are medium. Manifesto positions were not used.
